reviewScope: DR-133 provider-only-output-contract v1 only. This review does not mark DR-133 SATISFIED, open D-056 Class A, mint D-096 (A), authorize docs/v2/implementation/, apply or seal the candidate, or edit file 08 or COORD.
summary: REJECT at 1 blocker and 1 SHOULD-FIX. The live DR-133 acceptance cell and table header are quoted byte-exactly, the file-08 digest matches, all authority/status denials hold, and the artifact does not settle DR-131, DR-117, D9 values, or identity recipes. The core refusal evidence fails, however. NT-1 requires a 'well-formed TypeScript component payload' containing a finding object, but the effective TypeScript protocol is closed: the worker frame vocabulary has no Finding frame, FactBatchV1 and every payload are closed, unknown fields are provider-protocol, and FactCandidateV1 accepts only host-registry relation payloads. NT-1 therefore has no constructible input on the governing surface. The artifact also names findingLikeResult as forbidden and claims OBL-3 is covered by NT-1/2/3, yet no test defines or exercises a finding-like alias or a schema-valid smuggling attempt. Separately, the operative refusal triggers only the eight-member forbidden roster, which omits component-emitted rules, policy objects, and admission claims even though OBL-2 makes them host-owned; NT-2 tests only policyOutcome or verdict. A bounded successor can repair both defects by joining the effective DELIVERY protocol and retaining exact unknown-frame/unknown-field/provider-minted-schema mutation classes with existing provider-protocol handling, plus a closed reject rule for every non-fact/non-Coverage semantic product. DR-133 remains OPEN and this verdict authorizes nothing.

blockers.title: The required finding-refusal negative test is unconstructible on the governing TypeScript protocol and leaves finding-like smuggling untested
blockers.measurement: NT-1's input is 'A well-formed TypeScript component payload that includes at least one finding object.' The effective TypeScript provider surface does not admit such a payload. DELIVERY's unchanged protocol-major-1 wire schema has a closed worker-to-host frame vocabulary of HelloAck, UniverseAccepted, SnapshotAccepted, FactBatch, Coverage, Unavailable, BudgetExhausted, Complete, and Cancelled. Its frame envelope selects a closed payload schema; FactBatchV1 is closed to analysisOrdinal/stageId/batchIndex/facts/batchCommitment; each FactCandidateV1 is a closed host-registry fact candidate; and the decoder makes every unknown field provider-protocol with no ignore-unknown behavior. Adding a finding object therefore makes the payload malformed, not well-formed. The subject could instead mean a finding disguised inside a nominal FactCandidate, but it never defines findingLikeResult, never pins the host-owned relation/schema test that distinguishes that alias from a fact, and none of NT-1/2/3 exercises it. The subject's answeredAt claim for OBL-3 is consequently false at the exact boundary where the row requires retained negative tests.
counterexamples: Add a `findings` member to a canonical FactBatchV1 or CompleteV1 payload. DELIVERY rejects the unknown field before any subject-level 'well-formed finding payload' exists; NT-1 supplies no exact mutation site or oracle for this actual execution.

Put a finding-shaped byte object behind a provider-minted relationSchemaId or an otherwise mismatched canonicalRelationPayload in FactCandidateV1. The host-owned relation registry must reject it before fact admission, but the subject has no retained class for this schema-valid-envelope alias attack and no definition of findingLikeResult by which a test can recognize it.

Emit an unknown worker frame named Finding. The closed frame vocabulary rejects it as provider-protocol, but NT-1 does not name this constructible class or bind its pass oracle to the existing no-admission/discard behavior.
blockers.whyBlocker: DR-133's acceptance-evidence cell expressly requires component-emitted findings to be refused with retained negative tests. A negative class whose premise cannot be encoded on the governing surface, while the artifact's own alias category is undefined and untested, does not answer that required evidence. This is the central acceptance obligation, not optional fixture execution or a wording preference.
blockers.requiredRepair: In a successor, pin and join the effective DELIVERY TypeScript protocol without changing it. Replace NT-1 with constructible retained mutation classes at the existing boundary: at minimum an unknown Finding frame, a forbidden extra finding member on a named closed worker payload, and a FactCandidateV1 carrying a provider-minted/mismatched relationSchemaId or relation payload that attempts to masquerade as a finding-like result. Define the closed classification without inventing a finding schema: only host-validated FactCandidateV1 and CoverageResultV1 are semantic candidates, and no provider value is reinterpreted as a Finding. Each pass oracle must require rejection before admission, discard of uncommitted candidates, and the already-owned provider-protocol path where the binding protocol supplies it. Retain these as specified classes; execution may remain routed to the existing qualification gates. Mint no D9 value, payload surface, identity recipe, or implementation authority.

shouldFix.title: The refusal predicate is not closed over the host-owned rules, policy, and admission fragments it claims to answer
shouldFix.measurement: OBL-2 correctly declares rules, policy, findings, and admission host-owned, and OBL-1 says no semantic product other than facts/Coverage is admitted. But the operative refusal rule fires only when a payload contains an item in componentAdmittedOutputs.forbidden. That eight-member roster contains policyOutcome, verdict and planAdmission, but not a component-emitted rule, a policy object/threshold/waiver, or the broader admission claims represented by admissionOfFacts, admissionOfCoverage and admissionOfFindings. NT-2 tests only policyOutcome or verdict. The text therefore states ownership but leaves the reject-versus-ignore behavior for several named host-owned products outside its operative refusal and test rosters.
shouldFix.whyShouldFix: The exhaustive allowed-set prose makes the intended ownership boundary recoverable, so this is narrower than POOCV1-B1. Still, an implementer can follow the literal refusal predicate and silently ignore rather than refuse a rule/policy/admission claim, contrary to the review prompt's no-silent-fallback attack and the artifact's purpose of answering every fragment with a retained class.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Make the operative rule closed: every component semantic product outside host-validated fact candidates and Coverage candidates is refused, including rule definitions, policy/threshold/waiver objects, finding/admission claims, verdict/policyOutcome, and aliases. Either add an exact retained mutation class for the rule/policy/admission family or state and test how the effective DELIVERY unknown-field/frame closure subsumes it. Keep operational terminal/control observations distinct from semantic products.
